name: kernel-memory-samples
goal: Retain actual native and Wasm memory sample counts in kernel benchmark evidence

steps.title: Identify the failing behavior, expected behavior, and reproduction.
steps.evidence: Kernel memory observations contain actual values but omit samples, so mandatory performance validation correctly rejects them.

steps.title: Explain why existing standardized tests missed the bug; name the scenario, fixture, lifecycle or assertion gap and reusable test change.
steps.evidence: The normal kernel bench acceptance checks positive memory and runtime identity but never asserts memory sample counts. Extend those exact assertions before repair.

steps.title: Strengthen the existing standardized test; commit it before repair, run it failing with loop record --phase red, and preserve the assertion.
steps.evidence: Sealed red 89a0ec8a at f06c9b92f fails the unchanged normal kernel bench assertion: wasm memory sample count is undefined, expected 1.

steps.title: Implement the smallest repair without weakening the regression test.
steps.evidence: f601012f9 counts actual memory snapshots. Follow-up 90bc2e243 keeps unavailable native observations uncounted. Tests retain the same counted-memory assertion.

steps.title: Rerun the same unchanged regression test at a separate fix commit with loop record --phase green; preserve passing proof.
steps.evidence: Paired sealed green 7a68b25f at f601012f9 passes the same kernel bench test and frozen inputs. Current-source verification remains pending.

steps.title: Run relevant project checks and affected UI browser flows with fresh inspected screenshots and no unexpected browser errors; preserve diagnostics and keep pending until proof passes.
